title: Change the engine oil and filter
completeness: Covers draining the oil, cleaning the oil screens, refitting the plugs with their torques, changing the oil filter, filling with the correct oil and checking the level. The engine, gearbox and clutch share this oil.

required_tools.name: Pin wrench for the long oil screen

required_parts.name: Engine oil
required_parts.purpose: SAE 10W-50 fully synthetic four-stroke engine oil meeting JASO T903 MA2. About 1.0 l (1.1 US qt).

required_parts.name: Oil filter
required_parts.purpose: New.

required_parts.name: Seal rings and O-rings
required_parts.purpose: New seal ring for each magnetic drain plug, new O-rings where the plugs and cover need them.

prerequisites: Fresh oil, a new filter and new seal rings on hand.
critical_stop_conditions: Milky oil or metal flakes: stop and find the cause before running the engine.
Oil level not in the sight glass range: correct it before riding.
Never run the engine in a closed room: exhaust gas is poisonous.

steps.title: Note the starting point
steps.instruction: Write down the date and the engine hours. The engine oil, the oil filter and the oil screens are changed once after the first operating hour, then every 10 operating hours and after every race.

steps.title: Warm the engine
steps.instruction: Ride or run the engine until it is at operating temperature, then switch it off. Warm oil drains out much better.

steps.title: Park the bike level
steps.instruction: Park the bike on level ground. Wear gloves: the oil, the engine and the exhaust are hot.

steps.title: Put a drain pan under the engine
steps.instruction: Slide a drain pan under the engine, big enough for all the oil.

steps.title: Remove plug 1
steps.instruction: Unscrew and remove the magnetic oil drain plug with its seal ring. Only take out the plugs: leave the small screws next to them in place.

steps.title: Remove plug 2
steps.instruction: Unscrew and remove the screw plug with the oil screen and its O-rings.

steps.title: Let it drain
steps.instruction: Let all the oil drain out. Look at the oil and at the magnet as it drains.
verification: Oil colour and any debris noted.

branches.label: Metal flakes or milky oil
branches.condition: Do not just refill and ride: milky oil means coolant is getting in and flakes mean something is wearing. Record what you found and get the engine checked before running it.

steps.title: Clean the plugs and screens
steps.instruction: Clean the plugs, the oil screen(s), the magnet and the sealing faces on the engine.

steps.title: Push the oil screen back in
steps.instruction: Put the oil screen with its O-rings on a pin wrench, pass it through the plug hole on the opposite side of the engine case and push the screen all the way into the case.

steps.title: Refit plug 1
steps.instruction: Screw in the screw plug for the oil screen with its O-ring and tighten it to 15 N·m (11.1 lbf·ft).

steps.title: Refit plug 2
steps.instruction: Screw in the magnetic oil drain plug with a new seal ring and tighten it to 20 N·m (14.8 lbf·ft).

steps.title: Take off the filter cover
steps.instruction: Remove the oil filter cover screws and take off the cover with its O-ring.

steps.title: Pull out the old filter
steps.instruction: Pull the oil filter out of its housing (lock ring pliers help), let the housing drain, and clean the cover and the sealing faces.
verification: Old filter out, housing drained and clean.

steps.title: Pre-fill the filter housing
steps.instruction: Lay the bike on its side and fill the oil filter housing about one third full with fresh engine oil.

steps.title: Fill the new filter
steps.instruction: Fill the new oil filter with engine oil.

steps.title: Fit the new filter
steps.instruction: Push the new oil filter into the housing.

steps.title: Refit the filter cover
steps.instruction: Oil the O-ring of the filter cover, fit the cover and tighten the screws to 10 N·m (7.4 lbf·ft).

steps.title: Fill with fresh oil
steps.instruction: Stand the bike upright. Remove the filler plug and pour in 1.0 l (1.1 US qt) of SAE 10W-50 fully synthetic four-stroke engine oil meeting JASO T903 MA2. Too little oil, or poor oil, wears the engine fast.

steps.title: Refit the filler plug
steps.instruction: Refit the filler plug with its O-ring.

steps.title: Run it and check for leaks
steps.instruction: Start the engine outdoors or with good ventilation (exhaust gas is poisonous) and check the plugs and the filter cover for leaks. Then switch it off.

steps.title: Check the oil level
steps.instruction: Stand the bike upright on level ground. With the engine warm, wait 1 minute after switching off: the oil must sit between the middle and the top edge of the sight glass. With a cold engine it must reach the middle of the glass. If it is low, top up with the same oil.
verification: Level correct in the sight glass.

steps.title: Record the service
steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours, oil used and quantity. Take the old oil and filter to a recycling point.

entry_state: Bike on level ground, engine able to run.
exit_state: Fresh oil at the correct level, new filter, screens cleaned, no leaks, service logged.

steps.title: Fill the new filter

steps.title: Put a drain pan under the engine
steps.instruction: Slide a drain pan under the engine, big enough for all the oil.

steps.title: Remove plug 1
steps.instruction: Unscrew and remove the magnetic oil drain plug with its seal ring.

steps.title: Remove plug 2
steps.instruction: Unscrew and remove the other screw plug with its O-ring. Only take out the plugs: leave the small screws next to them in place.

steps.title: Remove plug 3
steps.instruction: Unscrew and remove the screw plug with the oil screen and its O-rings.

steps.title: Let it drain
steps.instruction: Let all the oil drain out. Look at the oil and at the magnet as it drains.
verification: Oil colour and any debris noted.

branches.label: Metal flakes or milky oil
branches.condition: Do not just refill and ride: milky oil means coolant is getting in and flakes mean something is wearing. Record what you found and get the engine checked before running it.

steps.title: Clean the plugs and screens
steps.instruction: Clean the plugs, the oil screen(s), the magnet and the sealing faces on the engine.

steps.title: Refit plug 1
steps.instruction: Screw in the screw plug with a new O-ring and tighten it to 15 N·m (11.1 lbf·ft).

steps.title: Push the oil screen back in
steps.instruction: Put the oil screen with its O-rings on a pin wrench, pass it through the plug hole on the opposite side of the engine case and push the screen all the way into the case.

steps.title: Refit plug 2
steps.instruction: Screw in the screw plug for the oil screen with its O-ring and tighten it to 15 N·m (11.1 lbf·ft).

steps.title: Refit plug 3
steps.instruction: Screw in the magnetic oil drain plug with a new seal ring and tighten it to 20 N·m (14.8 lbf·ft).

steps.title: Take off the filter cover
steps.instruction: Remove the oil filter cover screws and take off the cover with its O-ring.

steps.title: Pull out the old filter
steps.instruction: Pull the oil filter out of its housing (lock ring pliers help), let the housing drain, and clean the cover and the sealing faces.
verification: Old filter out, housing drained and clean.

steps.title: Pre-fill the filter housing
steps.instruction: Lay the bike on its side and fill the oil filter housing about one third full with fresh engine oil.

steps.title: Fit the new filter
steps.instruction: Push the new oil filter into the housing.

steps.title: Refit the filter cover
steps.instruction: Oil the O-ring of the filter cover, fit the cover and tighten the screws to 10 N·m (7.4 lbf·ft).

steps.title: Fill with fresh oil
steps.instruction: Stand the bike upright. Remove the filler plug and pour in 1.20 l (0.317 US gal) of SAE 10W-50 fully synthetic four-stroke engine oil. Too little oil, or poor oil, wears the engine fast.

steps.title: Refit the filler plug
steps.instruction: Refit the filler plug with its O-ring.

steps.title: Run it and check for leaks
steps.instruction: Start the engine outdoors or with good ventilation (exhaust gas is poisonous) and check the plugs and the filter cover for leaks. Then switch it off.

steps.title: Refit the skid plate
steps.instruction: Refit the skid plate.

steps.title: Check the oil level
steps.instruction: Stand the bike upright on level ground. With the engine warm, wait 1 minute after switching off: the oil must sit between the middle and the top edge of the sight glass. With a cold engine it must reach the middle of the glass. If it is low, top up with the same oil.
verification: Level correct in the sight glass.

steps.title: Record the service
steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours, oil used and quantity. Take the old oil and filter to a recycling point.

entry_state: Bike on level ground, engine able to run.
exit_state: Fresh oil at the correct level, new filter, screens cleaned, no leaks, service logged.

steps.title: Remove plug 1

steps.instruction: Clean the plugs, the oil screen(s), the magnet and the sealing faces on the engine.

steps.title: Refit plug 1
steps.instruction: Screw in the screw plug with a new O-ring and tighten it to 15 N·m (11.1 lbf·ft).

steps.title: Push the oil screen back in

steps.title: Refit plug 2

steps.title: Refit plug 3
steps.instruction: Screw in the magnetic oil drain plug with a new seal ring and tighten it to 20 N·m (14.8 lbf·ft).

steps.title: Take off the filter cover

steps.title: Pull out the old filter

steps.title: Pre-fill the filter housing

steps.title: Fit the new filter

steps.title: Refit the filter cover

steps.title: Fill with fresh oil

steps.title: Refit the filler plug
steps.instruction: Refit the filler plug with its O-ring.

steps.title: Run it and check for leaks
steps.instruction: Start the engine outdoors or with good ventilation (exhaust gas is poisonous) and check the plugs and the filter cover for leaks. Then switch it off.

steps.title: Record the service
steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours, oil used and quantity. Take the old oil and filter to a recycling point.

title: Clean and oil the air filter
completeness: Covers taking out the air filter, washing, drying and oiling it, cleaning the air box and intake flange, and refitting the filter and cover.

required_tools.name: Screwdriver or bit for the cover screw

required_parts.name: Air filter cleaning liquid
required_parts.purpose: For foam filters.

required_parts.name: Foam air filter oil
required_parts.purpose: For oiling the clean, dry filter.

required_parts.name: Long-life grease
required_parts.purpose: For the filter sealing edge.

prerequisites: Clean the outside of the bike first so no dirt falls into the air box.
critical_stop_conditions: Never run the engine without the air filter fitted.
Filter torn or not seated: dirt will get into the engine. Replace or refit it before riding.

steps.title: Note the starting point
steps.instruction: Write down the date and the engine hours. The air filter and air box are cleaned every 10 operating hours and after every race; check the filter before every ride and clean it sooner in dusty or muddy conditions.

steps.title: Take off the seat
steps.instruction: Remove the seat.

steps.title: Remove the cover screw
steps.instruction: If your air filter box cover is held by a screw, take the screw out. If it is not screwed, skip this.
verification: Screw out, or no screw fitted.

steps.title: Take off the air box cover
steps.instruction: Pull the air filter box cover free at its clips and lift it off.

steps.title: Release the retaining tab
steps.instruction: Unhook the tab that holds the air filter.

steps.title: Lift out the filter
steps.instruction: Lift the air filter out together with its support cage, then pull the filter off the support. Do not let dirt fall into the intake.

steps.title: Wash the filter
steps.instruction: Wash the foam filter thoroughly in air filter cleaning liquid and let it dry properly. Never use fuel or petrol: they attack the foam. Squeeze it to get the liquid out; never wring it.

steps.title: Oil the filter
steps.instruction: Oil the dry filter evenly with foam air filter oil.

steps.title: Clean the air box
steps.instruction: Clean the inside of the air filter box.

steps.title: Check the intake flange
steps.instruction: Clean the intake flange and check it for damage and that it sits tight.

branches.label: Flange damaged or loose
branches.condition: A damaged or loose intake flange lets dirt straight into the engine. Do not ride until it is fixed.

steps.title: Fit the filter on its support
steps.instruction: Fit the clean filter onto the support.

steps.title: Grease the sealing edge
steps.instruction: Spread long-life grease on the filter where it seals against the air box.

steps.title: Put the filter in
steps.instruction: Put the filter in the air box, with the retaining pin sitting in its bushing. A filter that is not seated lets dirt into the engine.

steps.title: Hook the tab back on
steps.instruction: Hook the retaining tab back on so it locks the filter in place.

steps.title: Refit the air box cover
steps.instruction: Fit the air filter box cover back on and make sure it clips in all round.

steps.title: Refit the cover screw
steps.instruction: If your cover is screwed, refit the screw and tighten it to 3 N·m (2.2 lbf·ft).
verification: Screw torqued, or no screw fitted.

steps.title: Refit the seat
steps.instruction: Refit the seat and check it is locked down.

steps.title: Record the service
steps.instruction: Write down the date and hours.

exit_state: Filter clean, oiled and seated, air box clean, cover secured, service logged.

steps.instruction: If your air filter box cover is held by a screw, take the screw out. If it is not screwed, skip this.
verification: Screw out, or no screw fitted.

steps.title: Take off the air box cover
steps.instruction: Pull the air filter box cover free at its clips and lift it off.

steps.title: Release the retaining tab
steps.instruction: Unhook the tab that holds the air filter.

steps.title: Lift out the filter
steps.instruction: Lift the air filter out together with its support cage, then pull the filter off the support. Do not let dirt fall into the intake.

steps.title: Wash the filter
steps.instruction: Wash the foam filter thoroughly in air filter cleaning liquid and let it dry properly. Never use fuel or petrol: they attack the foam. Squeeze it to get the liquid out; never wring it.

steps.title: Oil the filter
steps.instruction: Oil the dry filter evenly with foam air filter oil.

steps.title: Clean the air box
steps.instruction: Clean the inside of the air filter box.

steps.title: Check the intake flange
steps.instruction: Clean the intake flange and check it for damage and that it sits tight.

branches.label: Flange damaged or loose
branches.condition: A damaged or loose intake flange lets dirt straight into the engine. Do not ride until it is fixed.

steps.title: Fit the filter on its support
steps.instruction: Fit the clean filter onto the support with the marking on the support facing up.

steps.title: Grease the sealing edge
steps.instruction: Spread long-life grease on the filter where it seals against the air box.

steps.title: Put the filter in
steps.instruction: Put the filter in the air box with its marking facing up, with the retaining pin sitting in its bushing. A filter that is not seated lets dirt into the engine.

steps.title: Hook the tab back on
steps.instruction: Hook the retaining tab back on so it locks the filter in place.

steps.title: Refit the air box cover
steps.instruction: Fit the air filter box cover back on and make sure it clips in all round.

steps.title: Refit the cover screw
steps.instruction: If your cover is screwed, refit the screw and tighten it to 5 N·m.
verification: Screw torqued, or no screw fitted.

steps.title: Record the service
steps.instruction: Write down the date and hours.

title: Check, top up or change the coolant
completeness: Covers checking the antifreeze strength and level, topping up, and draining and refilling the coolant.

required_parts.name: Coolant
required_parts.purpose: Silicate-free coolant for aluminium engines with antifreeze protection to at least -25 °C (-13 °F); premixed coolant is easiest, and if you dilute it use distilled water, never plain water alone.

required_parts.name: Seal ring for the water pump drain screw
required_parts.purpose: New, when draining.

critical_stop_conditions: Never open the radiator cap on a hot engine.
Coolant in the engine oil or oil in the coolant: stop and have the engine checked.
Never fill with plain water only.

steps.title: Note the starting point
steps.instruction: Write down the date and the engine hours. Service interval: the antifreeze and level together once after the first operating hour, then every 10 operating hours and after every race.

steps.title: Let the engine cool
steps.instruction: Only work on a cold engine. Hot coolant is under pressure and can scald you if the cap is opened.

steps.title: Stand the bike upright
steps.instruction: Stand the bike upright on level ground.

steps.title: Take off the radiator cap
steps.instruction: Take off the radiator cap.

steps.title: Check the antifreeze
steps.instruction: Check the antifreeze strength with a coolant tester. It must protect in the range -25 to -45 °C (-13 to -49 °F). If it does not, correct the mix or change the coolant.

steps.title: Check the level
steps.instruction: Look into the radiator: the coolant must stand 10 mm (0.39 in) above the radiator fins.

branches.label: Level correct, coolant in good condition
branches.condition: Level right and the coolant is clean.

branches.label: Level low
branches.condition: Coolant below the mark but clean.

branches.label: Change is due or coolant dirty
branches.condition: Change interval reached, antifreeze wrong, or the coolant is dirty.

steps.title: Top up
steps.instruction: Top up with silicate-free coolant for aluminium engines with antifreeze protection to at least -25 °C (-13 °F); premixed coolant is easiest, and if you dilute it use distilled water, never plain water alone until the level is right. If you have to top up often, look for a leak.

branches.label: Topped up
branches.condition: Level now correct.

steps.title: Get ready to drain
steps.instruction: Stand the bike upright and put a container under the water pump cover.

steps.title: Drain the coolant
steps.instruction: Remove the drain screw on the water pump cover and let all the coolant drain out (the radiator cap is already off).

steps.title: Refit the drain screw
steps.instruction: Refit the drain screw with a new seal ring and tighten it to 10 N·m (7.4 lbf·ft).
verification: Drain screw torqued with a new seal ring.

steps.title: Fill with coolant
steps.instruction: Pour in silicate-free coolant for aluminium engines with antifreeze protection to at least -25 °C (-13 °F); premixed coolant is easiest, and if you dilute it use distilled water, never plain water alone until it stands 10 mm (0.39 in) above the radiator fins. The system takes about 0.95 l (1 US qt).

steps.title: Short test ride
steps.instruction: Refit the radiator cap, go for a short ride to work out air bubbles, then let the engine cool completely.

steps.title: Check the level again
steps.instruction: With the engine cold, take the cap off again and check the level (10 mm (0.39 in) above the fins). Top up if needed.

steps.title: Refit the radiator cap
steps.instruction: Refit the radiator cap firmly.

steps.title: Record the job
steps.instruction: Write down what you did (check, top-up or change), the date and hours. Take old coolant to a recycling point: it is poisonous.

exit_state: Coolant at the correct level with correct antifreeze strength, cap on, no leaks, job logged.

title: Check and correct the hydraulic clutch fluid level
completeness: Covers opening the clutch master cylinder reservoir, checking the fluid level and correcting it.
excluded: Changing or bleeding the clutch fluid

required_parts.name: Brake fluid
required_parts.purpose: DOT 4 / DOT 5.1. From a sealed container.

prerequisites: Clean the area around the reservoir first.
critical_stop_conditions: Brake fluid is harmful: keep it off skin and out of eyes, and wash spills off paint at once with water.
Fluid dark or contaminated: have it changed.

steps.title: Note the starting point
steps.instruction: Write down the date and hours. Service interval: the level is checked every 10 operating hours and after every race; the fluid is changed at least every 12 months.

steps.title: Level the reservoir
steps.instruction: Turn the handlebar so the clutch fluid reservoir on the handlebar sits level. Cover the paint around it with a rag: brake fluid eats paint.

steps.title: Open the reservoir
steps.instruction: Remove the cover screws and take off the cover with its rubber membrane.

steps.title: Check the fluid level
steps.instruction: Measure from the rim of the reservoir down to the fluid. It must be 4 mm (0.16 in) below the rim. The level rises as the clutch plates wear, so a high level is normal on a worn clutch.

branches.label: Level correct
branches.condition: Level as specified.

branches.label: Level wrong
branches.condition: Too high or too low.

steps.title: Correct the level
steps.instruction: Add or draw off brake fluid DOT 4 / DOT 5.1 until the level is right. Use fluid from a sealed container only.

steps.title: Close the reservoir
steps.instruction: Fit the membrane and cover and tighten the screws. Wipe up any spilled fluid at once with water.

steps.title: Record the job
steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours and whether fluid was added or removed.

entry_state: Bike on a lift stand, engine off.
exit_state: Chain clean and lubed, tension in range with the wheel straight, wear parts checked, job logged.
title: Check, clean and adjust the chain and sprockets
completeness: Covers cleaning and lubing the chain, measuring and setting the chain tension with wheel alignment, measuring chain wear, and checking the sprockets, chain sliders and chain guide with their torques.
excluded: Chain, sprocket, slider or guide replacement

required_tools.name: Spring scale or weight for the wear check

required_parts.name: Chain cleaner
required_parts.purpose: For removing old grease.

required_parts.name: Off-road chain spray
required_parts.purpose: For lubricating the clean, dry chain.

critical_stop_conditions: Never check or adjust the chain with the engine running.
Adjuster marks not equal on both sides: the wheel is crooked, do not ride.
Chain or sprockets worn past the limit, or slider worn through: replace before riding.
A chain that is too tight wears the gearbox and wheel bearings; too loose and it can come off and lock the rear wheel.

steps.title: Note the starting point
steps.instruction: Write down the date and hours. Check the chain before every ride. Service interval: chain tension once after the first operating hour, then every 10 operating hours and after every race; chain, sprockets and chain guide every 10 operating hours and after every race.

steps.title: Lift the rear wheel
steps.instruction: Engine off. Put the bike on a lift stand so the rear wheel hangs free. Never work on the chain with the engine running.
verification: Engine off, rear wheel off the ground.

steps.title: Check for caked dirt
steps.instruction: Look at the chain for thick dirt. If it is very dirty, clean it first.

branches.label: Very dirty
branches.condition: Mud or grit packed on the chain.

branches.label: Reasonably clean
branches.condition: No heavy dirt.

steps.title: Clean and lube the chain
steps.instruction: Rinse loose dirt off with a soft water jet, remove old grease with chain cleaner, let it dry, then spray on off-road chain spray. Keep cleaner and lube off the tyre and the brake disc.

steps.title: Measure the chain tension
steps.instruction: At the rear end of the chain slider, pull the top run of the chain upward and measure the gap. It must be 55-58 mm (2.17-2.28 in). The lower run must be tight while you measure. Chains wear unevenly, so turn the wheel and measure at several places.

branches.label: In range
branches.condition: Tension within the range everywhere.

branches.label: Out of range
branches.condition: Too tight or too loose.

steps.title: Loosen the axle nut
steps.instruction: Loosen the rear wheel spindle nut, then loosen the lock nuts on both chain adjusters.
verification: Axle nut and lock nuts loose.

steps.title: Set the tension
steps.instruction: Turn the adjusting screws on both sides by the same amount until the tension is right. The marks on the left and right adjusters must line up with the same reference marks, or the rear wheel will be crooked.
verification: Tension right, marks equal both sides.

steps.title: Lock it up
steps.instruction: Tighten the adjuster lock nuts, check the adjusters sit correctly on the adjusting screws, then tighten the spindle nut to 80 N·m (59 lbf·ft). Measure the tension again.

steps.title: Shift to neutral
steps.instruction: Shift the gearbox into neutral so the wheel turns freely.

steps.title: Look at the sprockets and chain
steps.instruction: Check the chain, rear sprocket and front sprocket for wear: hooked or pointed teeth, stiff or loose links. Replace chain and both sprockets together.

branches.label: Worn
branches.condition: Teeth hooked or chain damaged: fit a new chain and both sprockets before riding.

steps.title: Measure chain stretch
steps.instruction: Hang or pull 10-15 kg (22-33 lb) on the top run of the chain, then measure the length over 18 rollers on the bottom run. It must not be longer than 272 mm (10.71 in). Measure at several places; if any is over, the chain and both sprockets are worn out.

branches.label: Too long
branches.condition: Over the limit: fit a new chain and both sprockets before riding.

steps.title: Check the chain slider on the swingarm
steps.instruction: Look at the chain slider on top of the swingarm. If the bottom edge of the chain pins is level with or below the slider surface, it is worn out and must be replaced. Check it is tight and tighten its screws to 6 N·m (4.4 lbf·ft) with threadlocker (Loctite 243).

steps.title: Check the lower chain slider
steps.instruction: Check the chain sliding piece the same way: replace it if the chain pins are level with or below its surface. Check it is tight and tighten its screws to 15 N·m (11.1 lbf·ft).

steps.title: Check the chain guide
steps.instruction: Measure the thickness of the chain guide with a caliper. Replace it if it is thinner than 6 mm (0.24 in). Check it is tight and tighten its screws to 10 N·m (7.4 lbf·ft).

steps.title: Take the bike off the stand
steps.instruction: Take the bike off the lift stand.

steps.title: Record the job
steps.instruction: Write down the tension you found, any adjustment, and the wear checks.

critical_stop_conditions: Never check or adjust the chain with the engine running.
Adjuster marks not equal on both sides: the wheel is crooked, do not ride.
Chain or sprockets worn past the limit, or slider worn through: replace before riding.
A chain that is too tight wears the gearbox and wheel bearings; too loose and it can come off and lock the rear wheel.

steps.title: Note the starting point
steps.instruction: Write down the date and hours. Check the chain before every ride. Service interval: chain tension once after the first operating hour, then every 10 operating hours and after every race; chain, sprockets and chain guide every 10 operating hours and after every race.

steps.title: Lift the rear wheel
steps.instruction: Engine off. Put the bike on a lift stand so the rear wheel hangs free. Never work on the chain with the engine running.
verification: Engine off, rear wheel off the ground.

steps.title: Check for caked dirt
steps.instruction: Look at the chain for thick dirt. If it is very dirty, clean it first.

branches.label: Very dirty
branches.condition: Mud or grit packed on the chain.

branches.label: Reasonably clean
branches.condition: No heavy dirt.

steps.title: Clean and lube the chain
steps.instruction: Rinse loose dirt off with a soft water jet, remove old grease with chain cleaner, let it dry, then spray on off-road chain spray. Keep cleaner and lube off the tyre and the brake disc.

steps.title: Measure the chain tension
steps.instruction: At the rear end of the chain slider, pull the top run of the chain upward and measure the gap. It must be 55-58 mm (2.17-2.28 in). The lower run must be tight while you measure. Chains wear unevenly, so turn the wheel and measure at several places.

branches.label: In range
branches.condition: Tension within the range everywhere.

branches.label: Out of range
branches.condition: Too tight or too loose.

steps.title: Loosen the axle nut
steps.instruction: Loosen the rear wheel spindle nut, then loosen the lock nuts on both chain adjusters.
verification: Axle nut and lock nuts loose.

steps.title: Set the tension
steps.instruction: Turn the adjusting screws on both sides by the same amount until the tension is right. The marks on the left and right adjusters must line up with the same reference marks, or the rear wheel will be crooked.
verification: Tension right, marks equal both sides.

steps.title: Lock it up
steps.instruction: Tighten the adjuster lock nuts, check the adjusters sit correctly on the adjusting screws, then tighten the spindle nut to 80 N·m (59 lbf·ft). Measure the tension again.

steps.title: Shift to neutral
steps.instruction: Shift the gearbox into neutral so the wheel turns freely.

steps.title: Look at the sprockets and chain
steps.instruction: Check the chain, rear sprocket and front sprocket for wear: hooked or pointed teeth, stiff or loose links. Replace chain and both sprockets together.

branches.label: Worn
branches.condition: Teeth hooked or chain damaged: fit a new chain and both sprockets before riding.

steps.title: Measure chain stretch
steps.instruction: Hang or pull 10-15 kg (22-33 lb) on the top run of the chain, then measure the length over 18 rollers on the bottom run. It must not be longer than 272 mm (10.71 in). Measure at several places; if any is over, the chain and both sprockets are worn out.

branches.label: Too long
branches.condition: Over the limit: fit a new chain and both sprockets before riding.

steps.title: Check the chain slider on the swingarm
steps.instruction: Look at the chain slider on top of the swingarm. If the bottom edge of the chain pins is level with or below the slider surface, it is worn out and must be replaced. Check it is tight and tighten its screws to 10 N·m (7.4 lbf·ft) with threadlocker (Loctite 243).

steps.title: Check the lower chain slider
steps.instruction: Check the chain sliding piece the same way: replace it if the chain pins are level with or below its surface. Check it is tight and tighten its screws to 15 N·m (11.1 lbf·ft).

steps.title: Check the chain guide
steps.instruction: Measure the thickness of the chain guide with a caliper. Replace it if it is thinner than 6 mm (0.24 in). Check it is tight and tighten its screws to 10 N·m (7.4 lbf·ft).

steps.title: Take the bike off the stand
steps.instruction: Take the bike off the lift stand.

steps.title: Record the job
steps.instruction: Write down the tension you found, any adjustment, and the wear checks.

entry_state: Bike on a lift stand, engine off.
exit_state: Chain clean and lubed, tension in range with the wheel straight, wear parts checked, job logged.

title: Check the brakes: lever travel, discs, pads and fluid
completeness: Covers the front lever and foot brake free travel, disc wear, pad wear and security, and front and rear brake fluid levels with topping up.

required_tools.name: Spanners for the foot brake nuts

required_parts.name: Brake fluid
required_parts.purpose: DOT 4 / DOT 5.1. From a sealed container.

prerequisites: Clean the bike first so you can see the pads and the fluid windows.
critical_stop_conditions: Pads or discs past their limits: replace before riding.
Fluid below the mark: find the leak or worn pads before riding.
Brake fluid is harmful and eats paint: wear gloves and wash spills off with water.
Oil or grease on the discs or pads: clean the discs with brake cleaner; replace contaminated pads.

steps.title: Note the starting point
steps.instruction: Write down the date and hours. Check the brakes before every ride. Service interval: pads and discs every 10 operating hours and after every race; brake fluid changed at least every 12 months.

steps.title: Check the front lever free travel
steps.instruction: Push the front brake lever forward and feel the free play before it starts to work. It must be at least 3 mm (0.12 in). With no free play, pressure builds in the brake and it can drag and overheat. If it is wrong, set it with the lever reach adjusting screw (by hand only).

steps.title: Check the brake discs
steps.instruction: Measure the front and rear disc thickness at several points where the pads run. Front minimum 2.5 mm (0.098 in), rear minimum 3.5 mm (0.138 in). Also look for cracks, damage or warping. A worn or damaged disc must be replaced before riding.
verification: Both discs measured and looked at.

steps.title: Check the front fluid level
steps.instruction: Turn the handlebar so the front brake reservoir sits level and look at the sight glass: the fluid must not be below the mark. A dropping level means worn pads or a leak.

branches.label: Below the mark
branches.condition: Fluid below the mark in the sight glass.

branches.label: Level OK
branches.condition: Fluid at or above the mark.

steps.title: Top up the front brake
steps.instruction: Cover the paint. Remove the reservoir cover screws, take off the cover and membrane, and add brake fluid DOT 4 / DOT 5.1 until it is 5 mm (0.2 in) below the rim of the reservoir. Refit the membrane and cover. Wipe spills off at once with water. Find out why it was low.

steps.title: Check the front pads
steps.instruction: Look at the front brake pads. Replace both if the lining is thinner than at least 1 mm (0.04 in), or if a pad is cracked or damaged. Check the pads are held securely in the caliper.

steps.title: Check the foot brake free travel
steps.instruction: Unhook the brake pedal return spring, move the pedal back and forth between its stop and the point where it touches the master cylinder piston, and measure the free travel. It must be 3-5 mm (0.12-0.2 in). Hook the spring back on.

branches.label: In range
branches.condition: Free travel as specified.

branches.label: Out of range
branches.condition: Too much or no free travel.

steps.title: Set the foot brake free travel
steps.instruction: Unhook the return spring. Loosen the push rod lock nut and turn the push rod until the free travel is right; the pedal height itself is set with the stop screw and its nut. Hold the push rod and tighten its lock nut to 10 N·m (7.4 lbf·ft); hold the stop screw and tighten its nut to 20 N·m (14.8 lbf·ft). Hook the spring back on and check the free travel again.
verification: Free travel set, nuts tightened, spring on.

steps.title: Check the rear fluid level
steps.instruction: Stand the bike upright and look at the rear brake reservoir: the fluid must not be below the mark. If it is low, unscrew the cap with its membrane, add brake fluid DOT 4 / DOT 5.1 up to the mark, refit the cap, and find out why it was low.

steps.title: Check the rear pads
steps.instruction: Look at the rear brake pads. Replace both if the lining is thinner than at least 1 mm (0.04 in), or if a pad is cracked or damaged. Check they are held securely.

steps.title: Test the brakes
steps.instruction: With the bike on the ground, push it and apply each brake: both must bite firmly with no sponginess.

steps.title: Record the job
steps.instruction: Write down disc and pad measurements and any fluid added.

entry_state: Bike clean, upright on level ground, engine off.
exit_state: Lever free travel, discs, pads and fluid levels checked and in range, job logged.

title: Release built-up air from the fork and clean the dust boots
completeness: Covers releasing built-up pressure through the fork bleeder screws and cleaning and oiling the dust boots and fork tubes.

required_tools.name: Screwdriver or bit for the bleeder screw

required_parts.name: Universal oil spray
required_parts.purpose: For the dust boots and fork tubes.

prerequisites: Fork cold: do it before riding, not straight after.
critical_stop_conditions: Oil on the inner fork tubes or dripping from a boot: have the fork seals checked before riding.
Keep oil and cleaner off the brake disc.

steps.title: Note the starting point
steps.instruction: Write down the date and how the fork felt at the end of the last ride. Bleed the fork and clean the dust boots before every ride.

steps.title: Lift the bike
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a lift stand so the front wheel is off the ground and the fork hangs fully extended.

steps.title: Open the bleeder screws
steps.instruction: Loosen the bleeder screw at the top of each fork leg. Any built-up pressure hisses out.

steps.title: Close the bleeder screws
steps.instruction: Tighten the bleeder screws again.

steps.title: Take off the fork protectors
steps.instruction: Remove the fork protectors so you can reach the dust boots.

steps.title: Push the dust boots down
steps.instruction: Push the dust boot on each fork leg down off its seat. Dirt collects behind them and, left there, makes the fork seals leak.

steps.title: Clean and oil the boots and tubes
steps.instruction: Clean the dust boots and the inner fork tubes on both legs and oil them lightly with universal oil spray. Keep oil off the brake disc.
verification: Boots and tubes clean and oiled, disc clean.

steps.title: Refit the dust boots
steps.instruction: Press the dust boots back into their seats and wipe off the extra oil.
verification: Boots seated, extra oil wiped off.

steps.title: Refit the fork protectors
steps.instruction: Refit the fork protectors.

steps.title: Take the bike off the stand
steps.instruction: Take the bike off the lift stand.

steps.title: Record the job
steps.instruction: Note that the fork was bled and anything you saw: oil on the tubes means a seal is leaking.

entry_state: Bike clean, tyres at the right pressure, lift stand and a helper available.
exit_state: Shock and fork clickers at standard, sag measured, fork air at standard, baseline logged.
title: Set the suspension back to the standard baseline and check the sag
completeness: Covers setting the shock compression and rebound clickers to standard, measuring static and rider sag, setting the fork air pressure, and setting the fork clickers to standard.
excluded: Changing the shock spring preload or spring (shock removal)
critical_stop_conditions: Never set the fork air pressure outside the minimum and maximum.
Never force a clicker past its stop.
The shock holds high-pressure nitrogen: never take it apart.

steps.title: Write down your current settings
steps.instruction: Before changing anything, write down every clicker position (count the clicks while turning each one gently in to its stop, then turn it back out to where it was) and the fork air pressure if your fork has one. Then you can always go back.

steps.title: Check the rider weight
steps.instruction: The standard settings are for a rider of 75-85 kg (165-187 lb) in full riding gear. If you are well outside that range, the springs (and the fork air pressure) need changing, not just the clickers.

steps.title: Shock first, then fork
steps.instruction: Set the shock first, then the fork. Turn every adjuster gently by hand and never force it past its stop.

steps.title: Shock low-speed compression
steps.instruction: Turn the low-speed compression adjuster on the shock clockwise to its stop, then back out 15 clicks (standard). Clockwise is harder, counter-clockwise softer.

steps.title: Shock high-speed compression
steps.instruction: Turn the high-speed compression adjuster clockwise to its stop, then back out 2 turns (standard).

steps.title: Shock rebound
steps.instruction: Turn the rebound adjuster at the bottom of the shock clockwise to the last click you can feel, then back out 15 clicks (standard).

steps.title: Measure the rear unloaded
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a lift stand so the rear wheel hangs free. Measure from the rear axle straight up to the SAG mark on the rear fender. Write it down as A.

steps.title: Measure static sag
steps.instruction: Take the bike off the stand. With a helper holding it upright and nobody on it, measure axle to SAG mark again (B). A minus B is the static sag; standard is 35 mm (1.38 in).

steps.title: Measure rider sag
steps.instruction: In full riding gear, sit in your normal position with your feet on the footrests and bounce a few times so the bike settles. A helper measures axle to SAG mark (C). A minus C is the rider sag; standard is 105 mm (4.13 in).

branches.label: Sag right
branches.condition: Sag at or close to standard.

branches.label: Sag wrong
branches.condition: Clearly more or less than standard.

steps.title: Spring preload needs changing
steps.instruction: Sag that is off means the shock spring preload, or the spring itself, needs changing. The standard preload is 9 mm (0.35 in) of spring compression and the spring rate goes by rider weight (65-75 kg: 39 N/mm, 75-85 kg: 42 N/mm, 85-95 kg: 45 N/mm). The shock has to come off the bike to set it: do that as its own job or have a workshop do it. Small differences can be taken up with preload; large ones need a different spring.

steps.title: Let the fork settle
steps.instruction: Check the fork air only with the engine off for at least 5 minutes, and always under the same conditions. Put the bike on the lift stand so the fork is fully extended.
verification: Engine off long enough, fork extended.

steps.title: Set the fork air pressure
steps.instruction: Take the cap off the air valve on the left fork leg, push the fork pump together fully and connect it (a little air escapes into the hose, that is normal). The standard pressure is 10.3 bar (149 psi). Change it in steps of 0.2 bar (3 psi) and never go below 7 bar (102 psi) or above 12 bar (174 psi). Disconnect the pump and refit the cap by hand.

steps.title: Fork compression
steps.instruction: Turn the compression adjuster at the top of the fork clockwise to its stop, then back out 12 clicks (standard). If your fork has an adjuster on both legs, set both the same.

steps.title: Fork rebound
steps.instruction: Turn the rebound adjuster at the bottom of the fork clockwise to its stop, then back out 18 clicks (standard). If both legs have one, set both the same.

steps.title: Test ride
steps.instruction: Ride a familiar section slowly at first: suspension changes alter how the bike handles. Then make small changes one at a time from this baseline.

steps.title: Record the baseline
steps.instruction: Write down every setting, the sag figures and how the bike felt.

exit_state: Shock and fork clickers at standard, sag measured, fork air at standard, baseline logged.

steps.title: Check the rider weight
steps.instruction: The standard settings are for a rider of 75-85 kg (165-187 lb) in full riding gear. If you are well outside that range, the springs (and the fork air pressure) need changing, not just the clickers.

steps.title: Shock first, then fork
steps.instruction: Set the shock first, then the fork. Turn every adjuster gently by hand and never force it past its stop.

steps.title: Shock low-speed compression
steps.instruction: Turn the low-speed compression adjuster on the shock clockwise to its stop, then back out 15 clicks (standard). Clockwise is harder, counter-clockwise softer.

steps.title: Shock high-speed compression
steps.instruction: Turn the high-speed compression adjuster clockwise to its stop, then back out 2 turns (standard).

steps.title: Shock rebound
steps.instruction: Turn the rebound adjuster at the bottom of the shock clockwise to the last click you can feel, then back out 15 clicks (standard).

steps.title: Measure the rear unloaded
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a lift stand so the rear wheel hangs free. Measure from the rear axle straight up to the SAG mark on the rear fender. Write it down as A.

steps.title: Measure static sag
steps.instruction: Take the bike off the stand. With a helper holding it upright and nobody on it, measure axle to SAG mark again (B). A minus B is the static sag; standard is 35 mm (1.38 in).

steps.title: Measure rider sag
steps.instruction: In full riding gear, sit in your normal position with your feet on the footrests and bounce a few times so the bike settles. A helper measures axle to SAG mark (C). A minus C is the rider sag; standard is 105 mm (4.13 in).

branches.label: Sag wrong
branches.condition: Clearly more or less than standard.

steps.title: Spring preload needs changing
steps.instruction: Sag that is off means the shock spring preload, or the spring itself, needs changing. steps.title: Fork compression

steps.title: Fork rebound
steps.instruction: Turn the rebound adjuster at the bottom of the fork clockwise to its stop, then back out 12 clicks (standard). If both legs have one, set both the same.

steps.title: Test ride
steps.instruction: Ride a familiar section slowly at first: suspension changes alter how the bike handles. Then make small changes one at a time from this baseline.

steps.title: Record the baseline
steps.instruction: Write down every setting, the sag figures and how the bike felt.

title: Set the suspension back to the standard baseline and check the sag
completeness: Covers setting the shock compression and rebound clickers to standard, measuring static and rider sag, setting the fork air pressure, and setting the fork clickers to standard.
excluded: Changing the shock spring preload or spring (shock removal)
critical_stop_conditions: Never set the fork air pressure outside the minimum and maximum.
Never force a clicker past its stop.
The shock holds high-pressure nitrogen: never take it apart.

steps.title: Write down your current settings
steps.instruction: Before changing anything, write down every clicker position (count the clicks while turning each one gently in to its stop, then turn it back out to where it was) and the fork air pressure if your fork has one. Then you can always go back.

steps.title: Check the rider weight
steps.instruction: The standard settings are for a rider of 75-85 kg (165.3-187.4 lb) in full riding gear. If you are well outside that range, the springs (and the fork air pressure) need changing, not just the clickers.

steps.title: Shock first, then fork
steps.instruction: Set the shock first, then the fork. Turn every adjuster gently by hand and never force it past its stop.

steps.title: Shock low-speed compression
steps.instruction: Turn the low-speed compression adjuster on the shock clockwise to its stop, then back out 15 clicks (standard). Clockwise is harder, counter-clockwise softer.

steps.title: Shock high-speed compression
steps.instruction: Turn the high-speed compression adjuster clockwise to its stop, then back out 1.5 turns (standard).

steps.title: Shock rebound
steps.instruction: Turn the rebound adjuster at the bottom of the shock clockwise to the last click you can feel, then back out 15 clicks (standard).

steps.title: Measure the rear unloaded
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a lift stand so the rear wheel hangs free. Measure from the rear axle straight up to the SAG mark on the rear fender. Write it down as A.

steps.title: Measure static sag
steps.instruction: Take the bike off the stand. With a helper holding it upright and nobody on it, measure axle to SAG mark again (B). A minus B is the static sag; standard is 35 mm (1.38 in).

steps.title: Measure rider sag
steps.instruction: In full riding gear, sit in your normal position with your feet on the footrests and bounce a few times so the bike settles. A helper measures axle to SAG mark (C). A minus C is the rider sag; standard is 105 mm (4.13 in).

branches.label: Sag right
branches.condition: Sag at or close to standard.

branches.label: Sag wrong
branches.condition: Clearly more or less than standard.

steps.title: Spring preload needs changing
steps.instruction: Sag that is off means the shock spring preload, or the spring itself, needs changing. The standard preload is 8 mm (0.31 in) of spring compression and the spring rate goes by rider weight (65-75 kg: 39 N/mm, 75-85 kg: 42 N/mm, 85-95 kg: 45 N/mm). The shock has to come off the bike to set it: do that as its own job or have a workshop do it. Small differences can be taken up with preload; large ones need a different spring.

steps.title: Let the fork settle
steps.instruction: Check the fork air only with the engine off for at least 5 minutes, and always under the same conditions. Put the bike on the lift stand so the fork is fully extended.
verification: Engine off long enough, fork extended.

steps.title: Set the fork air pressure
steps.instruction: Take the cap off the air valve on the left fork leg, push the fork pump together fully and connect it (a little air escapes into the hose, that is normal). The pressure goes by rider weight: 65-75 kg: 10.1 bar (146.5 psi), 75-85 kg: 10.3 bar (149.4 psi), 85-95 kg: 10.5 bar (152.3 psi). Change it in steps of 0.2 bar (2.9 psi) and never go below 7 bar (102 psi) or above 12 bar (174 psi). Disconnect the pump and refit the cap by hand.

steps.title: Fork compression
steps.instruction: Turn the compression adjuster at the top of the fork clockwise to its stop, then back out 12 clicks (standard). If your fork has an adjuster on both legs, set both the same.

steps.title: Fork rebound
steps.instruction: Turn the rebound adjuster at the bottom of the fork clockwise to its stop, then back out 18 clicks (standard). If both legs have one, set both the same.

steps.title: Test ride
steps.instruction: Ride a familiar section slowly at first: suspension changes alter how the bike handles. Then make small changes one at a time from this baseline.

steps.title: Record the baseline
steps.instruction: Write down every setting, the sag figures and how the bike felt.

The standard pressure is 10.1 bar (146 psi). Change it in steps of 0.2 bar (3 psi) and never go below 7 bar (102 psi) or above 12 bar (174 psi). Disconnect the pump and refit the cap by hand.

steps.title: Fork compression
steps.instruction: Turn the compression adjuster at the top of the fork clockwise to its stop, then back out 12 clicks (standard). If your fork has an adjuster on both legs, set both the same.

steps.title: Fork rebound
steps.instruction: Turn the rebound adjuster at the bottom of the fork clockwise to its stop, then back out 12 clicks (standard). If both legs have one, set both the same.

steps.title: Test ride
steps.instruction: Ride a familiar section slowly at first: suspension changes alter how the bike handles. Then make small changes one at a time from this baseline.

steps.title: Record the baseline
steps.instruction: Write down every setting, the sag figures and how the bike felt.

entry_state: Bike clean, tyres at the right pressure, lift stand and a helper available.
exit_state: Shock and fork clickers at standard, sag measured, fork air at standard, baseline logged.
title: Set the suspension back to the standard baseline and check the sag
completeness: Covers setting the shock compression and rebound clickers to standard, measuring static and rider sag, setting the fork air pressure, and setting the fork clickers to standard.
excluded: Changing the shock spring preload or spring (shock removal)
critical_stop_conditions: Never set the fork air pressure outside the minimum and maximum.
Never force a clicker past its stop.
The shock holds high-pressure nitrogen: never take it apart.

steps.title: Write down your current settings
steps.instruction: Before changing anything, write down every clicker position (count the clicks while turning each one gently in to its stop, then turn it back out to where it was) and the fork air pressure if your fork has one. Then you can always go back.

steps.title: Check the rider weight
steps.instruction: The standard settings are for a rider of 75-85 kg (165-187 lb) in full riding gear. If you are well outside that range, the springs (and the fork air pressure) need changing, not just the clickers.

steps.title: Shock first, then fork
steps.instruction: Set the shock first, then the fork. Turn every adjuster gently by hand and never force it past its stop.

steps.title: Shock low-speed compression
steps.instruction: Turn the low-speed compression adjuster on the shock clockwise to its stop, then back out 15 clicks (standard). Clockwise is harder, counter-clockwise softer.

steps.title: Shock high-speed compression
steps.instruction: Turn the high-speed compression adjuster clockwise to its stop, then back out 2 turns (standard).

steps.title: Shock rebound
steps.instruction: Turn the rebound adjuster at the bottom of the shock clockwise to the last click you can feel, then back out 15 clicks (standard).

steps.title: Measure the rear unloaded
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a lift stand so the rear wheel hangs free. Measure from the rear axle straight up to the SAG mark on the rear fender. Write it down as A.

steps.title: Measure static sag
steps.instruction: Take the bike off the stand. With a helper holding it upright and nobody on it, measure axle to SAG mark again (B). A minus B is the static sag; standard is 35 mm (1.38 in).

steps.title: Measure rider sag
steps.instruction: In full riding gear, sit in your normal position with your feet on the footrests and bounce a few times so the bike settles. A helper measures axle to SAG mark (C). A minus C is the rider sag; standard is 105 mm (4.13 in).

branches.label: Sag right
branches.condition: Sag at or close to standard.

branches.label: Sag wrong
branches.condition: Clearly more or less than standard.

steps.title: Spring preload needs changing
steps.instruction: Sag that is off means the shock spring preload, or the spring itself, needs changing. The standard preload is 7 mm (0.28 in) of spring compression and the spring rate goes by rider weight (65-75 kg: 42 N/mm, 75-85 kg: 45 N/mm, 85-95 kg: 48 N/mm). The shock has to come off the bike to set it: do that as its own job or have a workshop do it. Small differences can be taken up with preload; large ones need a different spring.

steps.title: Let the fork settle
steps.instruction: Check the fork air only with the engine off for at least 5 minutes, and always under the same conditions. Put the bike on the lift stand so the fork is fully extended.
verification: Engine off long enough, fork extended.

steps.title: Measure the rear unloaded

steps.instruction: Take the bike off the stand. With a helper holding it upright and nobody on it, measure axle to SAG mark again (B). A minus B is the static sag; standard is 35 mm (1.38 in).

steps.title: Measure rider sag
steps.instruction: In full riding gear, sit in your normal position with your feet on the footrests and bounce a few times so the bike settles. A helper measures axle to SAG mark (C). A minus C is the rider sag; standard is 105 mm (4.13 in).

branches.label: Sag right
branches.condition: Sag at or close to standard.

branches.label: Sag wrong
branches.condition: Clearly more or less than standard.

steps.title: Spring preload needs changing
steps.instruction: Sag that is off means the shock spring preload, or the spring itself, needs changing. The standard preload is 8 mm (0.31 in) of spring compression and the spring rate goes by rider weight (65-75 kg: 42 N/mm, 75-85 kg: 45 N/mm, 85-95 kg: 48 N/mm). The shock has to come off the bike to set it: do that as its own job or have a workshop do it. Small differences can be taken up with preload; large ones need a different spring.

steps.title: Let the fork settle
steps.instruction: Check the fork air only with the engine off for at least 5 minutes, and always under the same conditions. Put the bike on the lift stand so the fork is fully extended.
verification: Engine off long enough, fork extended.

steps.title: Set the fork air pressure
steps.instruction: Take the cap off the air valve on the left fork leg, push the fork pump together fully and connect it (a little air escapes into the hose, that is normal). The standard pressure is 10.4 bar (151 psi). Change it in steps of 0.2 bar (3 psi) and never go below 7 bar (102 psi) or above 12 bar (174 psi). Disconnect the pump and refit the cap by hand.

steps.title: Fork compression
steps.instruction: Turn the compression adjuster at the top of the fork clockwise to its stop, then back out 12 clicks (standard). If your fork has an adjuster on both legs, set both the same.

steps.title: Fork rebound
steps.instruction: Turn the rebound adjuster at the bottom of the fork clockwise to its stop, then back out 12 clicks (standard). If both legs have one, set both the same.

steps.title: Test ride
steps.instruction: Ride a familiar section slowly at first: suspension changes alter how the bike handles. Then make small changes one at a time from this baseline.

steps.title: Record the baseline
steps.instruction: Write down every setting, the sag figures and how the bike felt.

steps.instruction: Turn the high-speed compression adjuster clockwise to its stop, then back out 2 turns (standard).

steps.title: Shock rebound
steps.instruction: Turn the rebound adjuster at the bottom of the shock clockwise to the last click you can feel, then back out 15 clicks (standard).

steps.title: Measure the rear unloaded
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a lift stand so the rear wheel hangs free. Measure from the rear axle straight up to the SAG mark on the rear fender. Write it down as A.

steps.title: Measure static sag
steps.instruction: Take the bike off the stand. With a helper holding it upright and nobody on it, measure axle to SAG mark again (B). A minus B is the static sag; standard is 35 mm (1.38 in).

steps.title: Measure rider sag
steps.instruction: In full riding gear, sit in your normal position with your feet on the footrests and bounce a few times so the bike settles. A helper measures axle to SAG mark (C). A minus C is the rider sag; standard is 105 mm (4.13 in).

branches.label: Sag right
branches.condition: Sag at or close to standard.

branches.label: Sag wrong
branches.condition: Clearly more or less than standard.

steps.title: Spring preload needs changing
steps.instruction: Sag that is off means the shock spring preload, or the spring itself, needs changing. The standard preload is 8 mm (0.31 in) of spring compression and the spring rate goes by rider weight (65-75 kg: 42 N/mm, 75-85 kg: 45 N/mm, 85-95 kg: 48 N/mm). The shock has to come off the bike to set it: do that as its own job or have a workshop do it. Small differences can be taken up with preload; large ones need a different spring.

steps.title: Let the fork settle
steps.instruction: Check the fork air only with the engine off for at least 5 minutes, and always under the same conditions. Put the bike on the lift stand so the fork is fully extended.
verification: Engine off long enough, fork extended.

steps.title: Set the fork air pressure
steps.instruction: Take the cap off the air valve on the left fork leg, push the fork pump together fully and connect it (a little air escapes into the hose, that is normal). The standard pressure is 10.1 bar (146 psi).. Disconnect the pump and refit the cap by hand.

steps.title: Fork compression
steps.instruction: Turn the compression adjuster at the top of the fork clockwise to its stop, then back out 12 clicks (standard). If your fork has an adjuster on both legs, set both the same.

steps.title: Fork rebound
steps.instruction: Turn the rebound adjuster at the bottom of the fork clockwise to its stop, then back out 12 clicks (standard). If both legs have one, set both the same.

steps.title: Test ride
steps.instruction: Ride a familiar section slowly at first: suspension changes alter how the bike handles. Then make small changes one at a time from this baseline.

steps.title: Record the baseline
steps.instruction: Write down every setting, the sag figures and how the bike felt.

title: Pre-ride check
completeness: Covers the checks to do before every ride: fluids, brakes, chain, tyres, spokes, fork, air filter, controls, fasteners and fuel.
prerequisites: Engine cold for the coolant check.
critical_stop_conditions: Any brake fault, low brake fluid, loose spokes or a damaged tyre: do not ride until it is fixed.

steps.title: Start the check
steps.instruction: Do this before every ride, on level ground with the engine off and cold. The bike must be in perfect condition before it is ridden.

steps.title: Engine oil level
steps.instruction: Stand the bike upright and check the engine oil in the sight glass.

steps.title: Front brake fluid
steps.instruction: Check the front brake fluid is not below the mark in the sight glass.

steps.title: Rear brake fluid
steps.instruction: Check the rear brake fluid is not below the mark.

steps.title: Front brake pads
steps.instruction: Check the front pads have lining left and are held securely.

steps.title: Rear brake pads
steps.instruction: Check the rear pads have lining left and are held securely.

steps.title: Brakes work
steps.instruction: Check both brakes work properly, feel firm and have their free play.

steps.title: Coolant level
steps.instruction: With the engine cold, check the coolant level.

steps.title: Chain dirt
steps.instruction: Check the chain for packed dirt; clean it if it is caked.

steps.title: Chain and sprockets
steps.instruction: Look over the chain, both sprockets and the chain guide for wear and damage.

steps.title: Chain tension
steps.instruction: Check the chain tension.

steps.title: Tyres
steps.instruction: Look over both tyres for cuts, damage and wear.

steps.title: Tyre pressure
steps.instruction: Check the tyre pressures with the tyres cold: off-road, front 1.0 bar (15 psi) and rear 1.0 bar (15 psi).

steps.title: Spokes
steps.instruction: Check the spoke tension: loose spokes badly affect safety.

steps.title: Fork dust boots
steps.instruction: Clean the dust boots on the fork legs.

steps.title: Bleed the fork
steps.instruction: Release built-up air from the fork legs with the bleeder screws.

steps.title: Air filter
steps.instruction: Check the air filter and clean it if needed.

steps.title: Controls
steps.instruction: Check all controls are set right and move smoothly.

steps.title: Nuts and bolts
steps.instruction: Check screws, nuts and hose clamps are tight.

steps.title: Fuel
steps.instruction: Check there is enough fuel.

steps.title: Ready to ride
steps.instruction: Fix anything you found before riding and note it in the log.

entry_state: Engine cold, bike on its stand.
exit_state: Bike clean and dry, brakes dried, moving parts and chain lubricated, bare metal protected.
title: Wash the bike and do the after-wash check
completeness: Covers washing without forcing water into sensitive parts, drying the brakes, warming the engine, and lubricating and protecting after the wash.

required_parts.name: Motorcycle cleaner
required_parts.purpose: For washing.

required_parts.name: Chain spray
required_parts.purpose: For the chain.

required_parts.name: Corrosion protection spray
required_parts.purpose: For bare metal, not discs or exhaust.

critical_stop_conditions: Brakes weak after washing: brake gently until they bite normally before riding hard.

steps.title: Seal the exhaust
steps.instruction: Plug the end of the exhaust so no water can get in.

steps.title: Rinse off loose dirt
steps.instruction: Rinse the loose dirt off with a soft water jet. Do not wash the bike in direct sun.

steps.title: Wash with bike cleaner
steps.instruction: Spray the dirty parts with motorcycle cleaner (on a wet bike, never a dry one) and work it in with a brush or a soft sponge and warm water.

steps.title: Careful with the pressure washer
steps.instruction: If you use a pressure washer, never aim it at electrical parts and connectors, throttle or clutch cables, bearings or seals, and keep the nozzle at least 60 cm (23.6 in) away. High pressure forces water in where it causes faults.

steps.title: Rinse and dry
steps.instruction: Rinse with a gentle spray of water and let the bike dry thoroughly.

steps.title: Unplug the exhaust
steps.instruction: Take the plug out of the exhaust.

steps.title: Dry the brakes
steps.instruction: Water and dirt make the brakes weak. Brake carefully several times to dry and clean the pads and discs.

steps.title: Warm it up
steps.instruction: Ride a short distance until the engine is warm so water in hidden places evaporates.

steps.title: Let water out of the controls
steps.instruction: Push back the rubber caps on the handlebar controls so trapped water can evaporate.

steps.title: Lubricate when cool
steps.instruction: Once the bike has cooled, lubricate all moving parts and pivots.

steps.title: Clean and lube the chain
steps.instruction: Clean the chain and spray it with chain lube.

steps.title: Protect bare metal
steps.instruction: Treat bare metal with a corrosion protection spray, but never the brake discs or the exhaust.

steps.title: Care for the plastics
steps.instruction: Wipe the plastic and powder-coated parts with a mild cleaning and care product.

steps.title: Look it over
steps.instruction: While it is clean, look for cracks, leaks and loose parts and note anything you find.
